definitions.explanation: The state of never having been married. Used on official forms and in formal contexts to indicate marital status.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はまだ{未婚|みこん}だ。
{未婚|みこん}の{母|はは}として{子|こ}どもを{育|そだ}てている。
examples.english: She is raising a child as an unmarried mother.

examples.japanese: {最近|さいきん}は{生涯|しょうがい}{未婚|みこん}のまま{過|す}ごす{人|ひと}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: Recently, more and more people are spending their entire lives unmarried.

notes:
A formal term used on official documents and in statistics. Distinct from {独身|どくしん}, which simply means single and can include divorced or widowed people.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {未婚|みこん}の{母|はは} (unmarried mother)
- {未婚率|みこんりつ} (unmarried rate)
- {生涯|しょうがい}{未婚|みこん} (lifelong single, never married)

USAGE:
{未婚|みこん} specifically means "never married" and contrasts with {既婚|きこん} (married). For someone who was previously married, {離婚|りこん} (divorced) or {死別|しべつ} (bereaved) would be used instead. On forms, the choices are typically {未婚|みこん} / {既婚|きこん}.
